messages:
mike: Headline: multiple Okta and AAD customers hit SSO failures after last night's KMS rekey. SCIM provisioning 403s and SAML role claims are missing for affected users. :rotating_light:

mike: Quick log snippet from provisioner: `ERROR: kms.decrypt failed: InvalidCiphertext: key id arn:aws:kms:...:alias/redwood-provision`

tanya: Ugh. did the rekey rotate alias or just underlying key material?

deploy-bot: deploy: KMS rekey rollout completed 2026-02-19T03:12Z. No rollbacks.

mike: It looks like the service that parses encrypted role extids still expects the old key context. Decrypt returns InvalidCiphertext for extids created before rotate. SCIM deprov tries to match and fails -> 403 from provisioner.

miranda-oncall: Confirmed impact: ~12 tenants seeing role mapping disappear, SCIM deprovision flapping. Correlation id 7f4b2c in logs. Temporarily toggled provisioner fallback to "accept-legacy-extid" for queued jobs.

sam: Is there any JWE/JWS difference? Okta assertions come with `urn:okta:claim:roles` mapping to our `extId` field which we encrypt when storing. If decrypt fails we treat as absent.

tanya: Looks like extid encryption used KMS encryption context with tenant_id. If alias rotated without preserving key id in alias rewrite path, ciphertext can't be decrypted by new key. Need to run re-encrypt/backfill.

mike: Workaround I pushed: small hotfix to provisioner to attempt `kms.decrypt` with `GrantTokens` and then log fallback event if fails, but not break provisioning. Patch link: https://git.internal/r/redwood/provisioner/commit/2b9f

miranda-oncall: Patch deployed to staging, rolling to prod in 5m. Will run controlled re-encrypt backfill for affected tenants during maintenance window.

sam: For the backfill use this pattern: `aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://encrypted.bin --context tenant=ACME` then re-encrypt with new key and replace. Script: ```bash
#!/bin/bash
set -e
for t in "$@"; do
  aws s3 cp s3://rb-extids/$t.enc /tmp/$t.enc
  plaintext=$(aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb:///tmp/$t.enc --encryption-context tenant=$t --query Plaintext --output text | base64 --decode)
  aws kms encrypt --key-id alias/redwood-provision-new --plaintext "${plaintext}" --encryption-context tenant=$t --output text > /tmp/$t.new
  aws s3 cp /tmp/$t.new s3://rb-extids/$t.enc --acl private
done
```

tanya: Nice. We'll need an allowlist for tenants we backfill first. Also update audit log entries to include `reencrypt: true` to track changes for compliance.

miranda-oncall: Agreed. action items: 1) run backfill for affected tenants tonight 2) notify their admins + SOC 3) add audit entries and add unit tests for decrypt-fallback behavior.

mike: Filing incident ticket and postmortem. Root cause hypothesis: rekey automation swapped alias pointing to new key but ciphertexts were created with a different key id/encryption-context binding that isn't compatible after rotation. We should change rotation process to preserve key lineage for decryption or perform in-place re-encrypt as part of rotation.

sam: FYI, I've added a short-term metric to alert on `kms.decrypt` InvalidCiphertext > 5/min to eng-sre and eng-security.

miranda-oncall: Thanks all. I'll coordinate customer comms and schedule the maintenance. Please ack with :thumbsup: when you have the runbook approved.

mike: :thumbsup:

tanya: :thumbsup:

sam: :thumbsup:
